checklist.notes: The decision, request, helper action, stress target, and four retell facts are directly identified.
A single short story is reused across noticing, dialogue, listening, and retelling, keeping integration manageable for A2.2.
Every section develops the same rain-and-books account toward a full result that can be passed to another listener.
The complete account and retell combine narrative sequence, make/made a decision, past framing, a help request, and movable information focus.
The lesson retrieves the foundation strands, embeds them in a cohesive request-and-result account, then adds listener-oriented mediation.
Cue lines, explicit stress contrasts, role switching, four factual listening prompts, and source comparison provide workable self-study scaffolding and checks.
Capitalized stress cues and role-based repetition are accessible supports without learner-group overgeneralization.
